claims.text: A combined cryo-rolling and controlled-annealing treatment can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with lamellar FCC/B2 phases in the as-cast state.
The as-cast lamellar structure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is inherently coarse.
Severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing near 600°C activates phase-selective recrystallization.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 while retaining its lamellar character.
The treated structure contains recrystallized fine grains specifically at phase boundaries.
The refined duplex structure produces a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
Refined grain boundaries hinder dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
Inherited lamellae and phase interfaces distribute deformation strain more effectively.
The hierarchical treated microstructure generates a microcrack-arresting mechanism that contributes to improved ductility.
Relative to the as-cast state, the treatment will increase both yield strength and elongation to failure.
The as-cast eutectic HEA typically has limited ductility and lower strength because of coarse lamellae.
The proposed treatment is expected to work under room-temperature, quasi-static tensile deformation.
The strategy is primarily applicable to eutectic HEAs having dual-phase lamellar structures such as FCC/B2.
Changes in rolling strain, annealing temperature, or alloy chemistry may prevent formation of the desired duplex refinement.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements depends on processing parameters and alloy composition.
A comparison of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 against material cryo-rolled to about 90% reduction and annealed near 600°C can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain statistically significant increases in both yield strength and ductility, or failure to observe the expected hierarchical microstructure, would refute the hypothesis.
